questions.question: Sobhit has purchased an article from Ronita at a discount of 10%. Still, Ronita earned a profit of Rs. 610 because the article was marked up by 350% above its cost price. Find the value of the discount offered by Ronita.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sobhit purchased an article from Ronita at a discount of 10%

Ronita earned a profit of Rs. 610

Marked up price = 350% above its cost price

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price = Cost Price [100 + Mark-Up%]%

Selling Price = Marked Price [100 - Discount%]%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit 

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the article be Rs. x

According to the question 

Marked Price of article by Ronita = x × (100 + 350)%

⇒ Marked Price of article by Ronita = 9x/2

Since, Discount Percent = 10% 

Selling Price = Marked Price [100 - Discount%]%

⇒ Selling Price = (9x/2) × (100 - 10)%

⇒ Selling Price = 81x/20

And also according to the question 

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit 

⇒ Selling Price of article = (x + 610)

Now, We can write

81x/20 = x + 610

⇒ 81x/20 - x = 610

⇒ 61x/20 = 610

⇒ x = 610 × (20/61)

⇒ x = 200

So, Marked Price = (9 × 200)/2 = Rs. 900

Discount% = 900 × 10% = 90

**∴ The value of discount offered by Ronita is Rs. 90.**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is ₹800. It is sold for ₹612.50, after two successive discounts each of x%. If a single discount of 2x% is given on the same marked price, then the selling price of the article will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The marked price of an article is ₹800. It is sold for ₹612.50, after two successive discounts each of x%.

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount/100) × (1 - Discount/100)

**Calculation:**

612.50 = 800 × (1 - x/100) × (1 - x/100)

⇒ 612.50 / 800 = (1 - x/100) × (1 - x/100)

⇒ 0.765625 = (1 - x/100)²

⇒ √0.765625 = 1 - x/100

⇒ 0.875 = 1 - x/100

⇒ x/100 = 1 - 0.875

⇒ x/100 = 0.125

⇒ x = 12.5%

If a single discount of 2x% is given:

2x = 2 × 12.5% = 25%

New Selling Price = 800 × (1 - 25/100)

⇒ New Selling Price = 800 × 0.75

⇒ New Selling Price = 600

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Suresh bought a cricket bat with 20 percent discount on the marked price. He sold the bat with 12 percent profit on the marked price. What was his per cent profit on the price he bought?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Marked Price (MP) of the bat be 100 units.

Cost Price (CP) for Suresh = 100 − 20% of 100 = 80 units.

Selling Price (SP) of the bat = 100 + 12% of 100 = 112 units.

Profit earned by Suresh = SP − CP = 112 − 80 = 32 units.

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (32 ÷ 80) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/897ecee88e8630d2f836ddda088534427121ec891c8a14454b3e8701a9f45f2b.png] 

**Given:**

Discount at which the bat was bought = 20% on Marked Price (MP)

Profit at which the bat was sold = 12% on Marked Price (MP)

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = MP − Discount

Selling Price (SP) = MP + Profit

Actual Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the Marked Price (MP) of the bat be 100.

⇒ Suresh's Cost Price (CP) = MP − 20% of MP

⇒ CP = 100 − 20 = 80

⇒ Suresh's Selling Price (SP) = MP + 12% of MP

⇒ SP = 100 + 12 = 112

⇒ Profit made by Suresh = SP − CP

⇒ Profit = 112 − 80 = 32

⇒ Profit percentage on the price he bought = (32 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (2 ÷ 5) × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Marked Price (MP) is the list price on which discounts are calculated. Unless specified otherwise, Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit or loss is generally calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated to be calculated on the Selling Price (SP). Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

The single equivalent discount for two successive discounts of a% and b% is given by the formula: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: The marked price of a car is Rs. 5,00,000. Under a scheme successive discount of 10% and 8% are offered on it. Find the total discount offered while selling the car under the given scheme.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total discount% = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100

Effective Discount% = 10 + 8 − (10 × 8) ÷ 100 = 18 − 0.8 = 17.2%

**Total Discount** = 17.2% of Rs. 5,00,000

Total Discount = (17.2 ÷ 100) × 5,00,000 = 17.2 × 5,000 = Rs. 86,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 86,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 5,00,000; First Discount = 10%; Second Discount = 8%.
**Formulas:** SP = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)% | Total Discount = MP − SP
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a627e7c865f4ce4d355be77f46baf360d9a570dfb54ec5ac7ab2874d8c566f8.png] 
⇒ Price after 1st discount = 5,00,000 × (90 ÷ 100) = Rs. 4,50,000
⇒ Price after 2nd discount (Final SP) = 4,50,000 × (92 ÷ 100) = 4,500 × 92 = Rs. 4,14,000
⇒ Total Discount = MP − Final SP = 5,00,000 − 4,14,000
⇒ Total Discount = Rs. 86,000
**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 86,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

**Marked Price** is the price printed on an item. **Discount** is always calculated on the Marked Price unless stated otherwise.

Successive Discounts

Two successive discounts of x% and y% are NOT equal to (x+y)%. They are equivalent to a single discount of [x + y − (xy/100)]%.</p

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 20% and 30% are given while selling an item. What is the ratio of the marked price to the selling price of the item?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

2 successive discounts of 20% and 30%

**Calculations:**

Let the Marked price be 100.

SP after 1st discount = 100 - 20 = 80

SP after 2nd discount = 80 - 30% of 80 = 80 - 0.3(80)

= 80 - 24 = 56

So, The Ratio

= 100 ∶ 56

= 25 ∶ 14

**∴ The Required ratio is 25 ∶ 14.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Formula used:

When 2 successive discounts X and Y are given -

Equivalent discount = (X + Y - XY/100)%

**Calculation:**

X = 20% and Y = 30%

Equivalent discount = [20 + 30 - (20 × 30)/100]%

= 50 - 6

= 44%

Let MP be 100

Then, after 44% discount

SP = 56

∴ MP : SP = 100 : 56

= 25 : 14

∴ **Required ratio is 25 : 14**

questions.question: A sofa-set is offered for sale at three successive discounts of 10%, 5%, and 2%. Find the net selling price of the sofa-set, if its marked price is ₹18,000.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Selling Price can be calculated directly by multiplying the Marked Price with the respective discount multiplying factors.

Net SP = 18000 × 0.90 × 0.95 × 0.98

Net SP = 16200 × 0.95 × 0.98 = 15390 × 0.98 = 15082.20

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,082.20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31c18bf428cc434e99c9f4533ac0a8b572d94e62ce753025d39b67b93c7fc69b.png] 

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹18,000

Successive Discounts = 10%, 5%, and 2%

**Formula Used:**

Net Selling Price = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100) × (1 − D₃/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Net Selling Price = 18000 × (1 − 10/100) × (1 − 5/100) × (1 − 2/100)

⇒ Net Selling Price = 18000 × (90/100) × (95/100) × (98/100)

⇒ Net Selling Price = 18000 × (9/10) × (19/20) × (49/50)

⇒ Net Selling Price = 18000 × (8379 / 10000)

⇒ Net Selling Price = 1.8 × 8379

⇒ Net Selling Price = 15082.20

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,082.20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Marked Price (MP) is the maximum retail price displayed on the product. Selling Price (SP) is the amount at which the item is actually sold. SP = MP − Discount.

Discount Percentage Calculation

Discount is strictly calculated on the Marked Price of an article. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

questions.question: If the selling price of a bed is Rs. 21384 after allowing two successive discounts of 12% and 10%. Find the market price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discount ratio: 12% = 3/25 and 10% = 1/10.

Effective ratio (MP : SP) = (25 × 10) : (22 × 9) = 250 : 198.

Given SP = 198 units = Rs. 21384.

1 unit = 21384 ÷ 198 = Rs. 108.

Marked Price (250 units) = 250 × 108 = Rs. 27,000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 27,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Selling Price** (SP) = Rs. 21384, **Discount₁** = 12%, **Discount₂** = 10%.

**Formula Used:** SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e26b52e7da3bcf98cc92bd3f3c9939ce1d0f174177e7f0bf6efaaaa18e6b1aeb.png] 

⇒ 21384 = MP × (1 − 12/100) × (1 − 10/100)

⇒ 21384 = MP × (88/100) × (90/100)

⇒ 21384 = MP × (0.88 × 0.9)

⇒ 21384 = MP × 0.792

⇒ MP = 21384 ÷ 0.792

⇒ MP = 27000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 27,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is [a + b − (ab/100)]%.

Relationship between MP and SP

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. Also, SP = MP × (100 − d%)/100.

Marked Price (List Price)

It is the price displayed on the product before any discount is applied. MP = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100.</p
